the event time in a liquid Argon TPC can be determined with high accuracy using only a single parameter, and the precision of this time measurement is not dependent on the number of photodetectors in the detector, but rather the precision of the optical model.

(a) the event time in LAr TPCs can be measured by fitting the light pattern to the reconstructed tracks, (b) the method can be calibrated in-situ with data, (c) the method can achieve the same time precision as conventional warm liquid detectors with significantly lower photodector coverage.

the time of a neutrino interaction in a liquid argon detector can be measured with an error of about 1 ns with only 1% coverage of the detector with PMT's, and the error can be improved with better coverage.
